title: Eye of Providence, Masonic usage, Wedjat, and The Alan Parsons Project 'Eye in the Sky': source-grounded comparative note

subjects: Ancient Egyptian Wedjat / Eye of Horus
Masonic use of the all-seeing eye
Eye above unfinished pyramid on the reverse of the Great Seal of the United States
The Alan Parsons Project, Eye in the Sky (1982)
scope.question: Which visual and conceptual similarities are documented, which are later reuses, and which proposed historical connections remain unsupported?

wedjat.museum_description_summary: The Met describes the wedjat as combining human and falcon eye elements; in myth the eye is injured or stolen by Seth and restored by Thoth. The amulet embodies healing and rebirth/regeneration and was used protectively.

eye_of_providence.identity: Eye representing divine Providence / divine oversight, commonly enclosed in a triangle and surrounded by rays or glory.

great_seal_history.official_design_context: The 1782 Great Seal reverse specifies an unfinished pyramid and, in the zenith, an eye in a triangle surrounded with glory.
great_seal_history.designer_lineage_summary: Pierre Du Simitière proposed an Eye of Providence in a radiant triangle in the first committee; William Barton later proposed a pyramid and eye; Charles Thomson combined the elements in the final design.
great_seal_history.official_symbolism_summary: The pyramid signified strength and duration; the eye and Annuit Coeptis referred to providential favor/interpositions for the American cause.

masonic_usage.summary: Masonic sources use the all-seeing Eye of Providence as a reminder of the watchfulness or omniscience of the Great Architect and moral accountability.
masonic_usage.scottish_rite_position: The Scottish Rite states that the Great Seal is not a Masonic emblem; although the all-seeing eye is used by Masons and others, the eye combined with a pyramid has no official Masonic meaning and has not been adopted by a grand lodge as such.

alan_parsons_project_eye_in_the_sky.official_concept_summary: The official project site says the album concept concerns belief systems and the universal idea that someone is looking down on us, while also noting military and surveillance uses of the expression 'eye in the sky'. Eric Woolfson recalled a Las Vegas casino surveillance system called the 'eye in the sky'.

cover_symbol.claim_firewall: The official APP page displays the cover and explains the album concept but does not, in the retrieved text, explicitly label the cover glyph 'Eye of Horus'. The identification is therefore recorded as a high-confidence visual/secondary-source classification rather than as an official textual statement.

alan_parsons_project_eye_in_the_sky.comparative_value: This album is a documented modern cultural case in which a Wedjat/Eye-of-Horus-like emblem is paired with themes of belief, observation and surveillance. It demonstrates modern recontextualization, not ancient-to-modern secret-code continuity.

comparison_matrix.feature: divine omniscience/moral watchfulness as primary documented meaning

lineage_assessment.interpretation: Visual similarity and later reuse must be separated from documentary historical descent. The APP album provides a modern intentional/reception bridge around the motif of an observing eye, but it does not retroactively establish a Masonic or Providence-to-Wedjat lineage.

relationship_to_wedjat_binary_experiment.reason: These are culturally later symbols or reuses and must not contaminate the ancient museum-object geometry corpus.

highest_admissible_claim: The Wedjat, the Eye of Providence, Masonic all-seeing-eye usage, the Great Seal eye-over-pyramid composition, and the 1982 Alan Parsons Project 'Eye in the Sky' cover share an eye motif but belong to distinguishable historical and semantic contexts. Freemasonry uses an all-seeing Eye of Providence, while the Scottish Rite explicitly rejects the Great Seal eye-plus-pyramid as an official Masonic emblem. The Alan Parsons Project's official site ties 'Eye in the Sky' to belief, observation and surveillance; the cover is widely identified by secondary sources as the Eye of Horus/Wedjat. This is evidence of modern cultural reuse, not proof of a direct ancient-to-Masonic lineage or of hidden binary/Python encoding.
next_gate: Keep the APP and Providence/Masonic examples as modern iconographic controls. Execute the separately frozen museum-only Wedjat geometry protocol on exact SHA-256-sealed museum images before any comparison to later cultural symbols.
